reasons: mean attributable CPU contention 2.25 cores over 79 samples at or above the busy threshold 2.00 cores (25% of 8 logical CPUs)
run_conditions.busy_threshold_basis: performance-core count (hw.perflevel0.physicalcpu, else hw.physicalcpu); applied to the 1-min load average at the start only
run_conditions.load_average_end_note: informational only, not part of the rule: the 1-min load average is an EWMA of runnable threads, and after minutes of tight APFS / reaper / CoreML loops it mostly reflects the benchmark's own threads; user_contention measures other programs

user_contention.method: background sampler, one process listing per interval: proc_listallpids + proc_pid_rusage(RUSAGE_INFO_V1) per (pid, start time); per interval, the user+system CPU delta of every readable process (in practice the processes of the same user) plus the rise of its reaped-children CPU (ri_child_user_time + ri_child_system_time; a tracked child's last cumulative CPU is matched first, so nothing is counted twice), excluding this benchmark process and its descendants (bench_child), divided by the interval; a process that started during the run counts from its start; mean is time-weighted (attributable core-seconds / sampled seconds), p95 and max are over the per-interval values; a reaped child's CPU is credited in the interval its parent reaps it
user_contention.not_attributed: processes of other users (root and system daemons such as kernel_task, mds, fseventsd, aned, ANECompilerService are unreadable; see external_cpu_total); CPU a process spends after the last listing that saw it unless a readable parent reaps it; short processes whose parent is unreadable (launchd) or reaps them after the run

processes.method: proc_listallpids + proc_pid_rusage(RUSAGE_INFO_V1) per (pid, start time) at every sample, names from proc_name (else proc_pidpath); cpu_seconds = own CPU + reaped-children CPU credited during the run; processes of other users are usually unreadable and are counted, not attributed

external_cpu_total.note: informational, not part of the rule: system busy cores minus this process's own cores includes unattributable root and system services (kernel_task, mds, fseventsd, aned, ANECompilerService), which mostly respond to the benchmark's own filesystem (clonefile trees, deletions, FSEvents) and CoreML activity; user_contention measures interference from other programs
external_cpu_total.method: system busy cores = (user+system+nice tick delta / all-tick delta) x logical CPUs from host_statistics(HOST_CPU_LOAD_INFO); own cores = getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) user+system CPU delta / interval; external cores = max(0, system - own); mean is time-weighted over the sampled intervals; unattributed core-seconds = external core-seconds - attributed core-seconds (readable processes including the benchmark's descendants; may be slightly negative from tick vs rusage accounting)

run_conditions.rule: preliminary when reduced-scale; when the 1-min load average at the start (after --quiet-wait) is above the busy threshold (performance-core count); when the time-weighted mean attributable CPU contention over the run is at or above 25% of the logical CPUs (attributable contention = user+system CPU of the other processes the benchmark can read, in practice same-user processes, from proc_listallpids + proc_pid_rusage per (pid, start time) about once per second, including CPU of children they reaped, excluding the benchmark process and its descendants, divided by the sampled seconds); when that contention could not be measured (CPU sampler failed or recorded no samples, no process listing succeeded, a listing failed, or an interval has no attribution); or when the measured sources changed during the run. Informational only: the end-of-run load average (it mostly reflects the benchmark's own threads) and external_cpu_total (system busy cores from host_statistics minus this process's getrusage), which includes unattributable root and system services (kernel_task, mds, fseventsd, aned) that mostly respond to the benchmark's own filesystem and CoreML activity. Only a run that is not preliminary decides the phase result (T18)

targets_note: Rows 1-4 measure WarmBranchPool::acquire on a warm hit: one renameatx_np(RENAME_EXCL) of a standby cloned earlier, p50 0.1067-0.1497 ms across 4 fixtures (960 hits, 0 misses; a row passes only without misses). The gated acquire and rollback rows are timed with the pool idle (settle before each acquire, rollback after the refill finished); the contended cases are reported next to them. The pool does not make clonefile cheaper: a cold clonefile is still O(entries) inside the kernel, p50 0.176 ms at 9 files and 7.321 ms at 1025 files, with getrusage ru_stime of 6.95-15.17 us per tree entry, and every acquire is paid for by one refill clone off the caller's path (standby replenish p50 1.097 ms small, 7.247 ms medium). An acquire right after a commit finds the standby stale: at medium 8/60 fell back to a cold clone and 52/60 waited for the refill in flight, p50 10.158 ms. A commit or rollback issued while the refill clone runs waits behind it (small: commit 1.463 ms, rollback 1.072 ms p50). The commit row times the RENAME_SWAP syscall (small p50 0.130 ms); the caller-visible commit (lock, checks, swap, version) has p50 0.472 ms. The online-model rows time back-to-back calls (cpuAndNeuralEngine p50 0.181 ms, cpuOnly 0.229 ms). One call after a 3.0 ms gap takes 0.360 ms with the CPU busy in the gap and 0.674 ms with it idle (cpuOnly 0.238 / 1.529 ms: cpuAndNeuralEngine is slower than cpuOnly with a busy CPU, speedup 0.66, and faster with an idle CPU, speedup 2.27). The end-to-end ane_score stage, one call per transaction, has p50 0.395 ms, 2.18x the back-to-back p50 and 1.10x the busy-gap isolated p50. Live-tree integrity: 30/30 checks passed, stores clean: true. One run on Apple M2, 11/11 gated rows passed. This run is PRELIMINARY (mean attributable CPU contention 2.25 cores over 79 samples at or above the busy threshold 2.00 cores (25% of 8 logical CPUs)); only a quiet full-scale run decides the phase result; the end-of-run load average and the total external CPU (system minus own: mean 4.11 cores, 146.58 core-seconds unattributed, mostly root and system services responding to the benchmark's own filesystem and CoreML activity) are informational.
